headline: Dollar closes higher near $930 as Brent oil tops US$100 amid naval war in the Strait of Hormuz | Diario Financiero
summary: The dollar closed higher near 930 as Brent crude rose above $100 a barrel amid a naval war in the Strait of Hormuz. Copper in London traded above $6.7 per pound.
why: Brent is the global benchmark for crude oil, and the Strait of Hormuz carries a large share of seaborne oil trade, so disruptions there move energy prices and inflation expectations worldwide.
why_moved: The report links the rise in Brent above $100 to a naval war in the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil transit route. Tariff expectations and tight copper supply are also cited in the input.
